text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Minister of Finance Aivar Kreituss announced that today he will tender his resignation to Prime Minister Andris Shkele. He said that he may start a new political party in parliament.
- The parliament's budget and finance committee has approved the 1997 budget for approval at the first reading.

- President Guntis Ulmanis met Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs and Defence Minister Andrej Krastinsh. They approved a programme of measures to increase Latvia's readiness for joining NATO. Ulmanis announced that he will ask parliament to allocate more funds for the development of the Latvian armed forces to meet NATO standards.
- Shkele blames officials for negligence who switched Latvia to winter tiem one month ahead of the rest of Europe.
- No substantial progress was achieved yesterday in talks between Latvia and Russia on the delimitation of land borders. Both sides said they were ready to seek a compromise.

- The television company IGE went on strike, refusing to start broadcasting on the second national TV channel in protest against unfair competition in the Latvian TV market and 'chaos and corruption' in the advertising sphere'.

- Riga City Council approved new tariffs for medical services which will be effective beginning October 1. To visit a doctor, a patient is to pay one lat and to visit a medical nurse will cost 0.40 lats.
- The EBRD and the World Bank are interested in investing money in Latvia, particularly in the privatisation of large energy companies such as Latvenergo and Latvijas Gaze.
